Typical messages include confirmations, reminders, reschedules, building/parking instructions, and follow-ups. No promotional blasts or affiliate marketing. Who Sends the Messages Messages are sent by Leasey.AI on behalf of the specific property manager or company you contacted (referred to as [Client Name] ). Who Receives the Messages Individuals who expressly opt in to receive SMS related to their rental inquiry with [Client Name] . Geography Available to recipients in the United States and Canada . U.S. messages are sent via A2P 10DLC long code numbers; Canadian messages are sent via local long code or toll-free numbers. Message Frequency Message frequency varies by conversation (typically 1–6 messages per inquiry). Charges Message & data rates may apply. Check your mobile plan for details. How to Opt In (Consent) You may opt in through one or more of the following methods: Website / Form Opt-In (recommended): When you submit a listing inquiry or book a tour, you provide your mobile number and check an unchecked consent box next to the following statement: “I agree to receive SMS about my rental inquiry from [Client Name] via Leasey.AI . Message frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help. ” The form links to this page, our Terms , and Privacy Policy . Text-to-Join (optional): Text LEASE or TOUR to +1 XXX-XXX-XXXX to start a conversation about your inquiry with [Client Name] . You will immediately receive an opt-in confirmation that includes brand identification, how to get help, how to opt out, and a link to this page. Verbal/Phone Consent (with confirmation): If consent is given by phone or in person, we send a confirmation SMS. In some cases we use double opt-in (we ask you to reply YES to confirm) before sending additional messages. Marketplace/Partner Leads: If your inquiry originates from a marketplace or partner form where SMS consent cannot be verified, we use double opt-in : our first message asks you to reply YES to continue . We won’t message you again unless you reply YES . Consent is not a condition of purchase, lease, or rental. We maintain timestamped records of consent (form IP/time, keyword or YES reply, and opt-out history). What You’ll Receive Tour scheduling links, confirmations, reminders, and reschedules Building entry and parking instructions Follow-ups to answer questions about the unit or application Links Policy: When links are included, they use leasey.ai or client-owned domains. We do not use public URL shorteners (e.g., bit.ly, tinyurl). How to Opt Out You can stop messages at any time by replying STOP . We will send one final message to confirm your opt-out, and you will no longer receive texts for that conversation/client. Recognized opt-out keywords also include: STOP, CANCEL, END, QUIT, UNSUBSCRIBE . If you’ve opted into multiple conversations with different clients, reply STOP in each respective thread. How to Get Help Reply HELP at any time for assistance. You can also contact support at info@leasey.ai . Delivery & Liability Delivery may be affected by carrier coverage and network conditions. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Privacy & Data Use We use your mobile number only to provide this messaging service for your inquiry. We do not sell or share mobile numbers for third-party marketing. We may share data with service providers (e.g., messaging carriers) solely to deliver the service. See our full Privacy Policy for details on data retention, security, and your rights. Program Keywords (if applicable) Opt-in keywords: LEASE , TOUR Opt-out keywords: STOP , CANCEL , END , QUIT , UNSUBSCRIBE Help keyword: HELP Sample Program Messages “ Leasey.AI for [Client Name]: Thanks for your inquiry about [123 Main St #2B] . Want to schedule a tour? Reply with a day/time. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help.” “[Client Name] reminder: Your showing at [123 Main St] is [Today 4:30 PM] . Directions & notes: ** https://app.leasey.ai/s/[token]**.” “[Agent Name], [Client Name]: I need to move our showing to [Tomorrow 3:00 PM] . You can reschedule here: ** https://app.leasey.ai/s/[token]**.” “[Agent Name], [Client Name]: I’m in the lobby at [Building Name] . Visitor parking is beside [Entrance B] . Text when you arrive.” Compliance We operate this program in accordance with applicable U.S. and Canadian requirements, including CTIA guidelines , U.S. TCPA obligations, and Canada’s Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) consent and unsubscribe standards. Changes to This Program We may update program details from time to time. The “Last updated” date reflects the most recent changes. Operational Start Leasey.AI launched its MVP pilot with more than 30 landlords in 2021, prior to the formal incorporation of Silver Homes Technology Inc., with the founders committing full-time in February 2022 after securing the first enterprise client. Languages — Platform UI The Leasey.AI platform user interface is available in English. Languages — AI Agents Leasey.AI’s chatbot and AI phone agent support English, Spanish, French, and additional languages, with coverage expanding over time. Business Overview Founding Story Juan Leal and Carlos Leal founded Leasey.AI after experiencing firsthand the inefficiencies of residential property management while managing 12 rental properties in Vancouver. Both founders had backgrounds in management consulting — Juan at KPMG and Carlos at EY — and Carlos identified the same operational problems while advising some of Canada’s largest asset managers. Existing software at the time addressed only individual pain points, requiring property managers to stitch together multiple platforms and still rely on spreadsheets and email for core leasing work. The Leasey.AI team began building the platform part-time during the pandemic, running an MVP pilot with more than 30 landlords in 2021. Juan Leal and Carlos Leal committed to Leasey.AI full-time in February 2022 after securing the company’s first enterprise client. Every feature was co-designed with active customers: the team would put wireframes in front of clients, collect feedback, and ship updates rapidly, often within a week of identifying a new pain point. Core Identity Leasey.AI operates as a front-office leasing automation layer that sits alongside, not instead of, a property management system. The platform manages the full leasing process from the moment a unit becomes vacant through to a signed lease and the start of active lease management, while accounting, rent collection, and maintenance workflows remain in the operator’s existing PMS. Leasey.AI is operated by Silver Homes Technology Inc., a Canadian company with operations in Canada and the United States. Market Position Leasey.AI is designed for residential property managers and operators running portfolios of 100 or more doors. The platform targets professional operators — multifamily owners, single-family rental portfolios, student housing, senior living, co-living, and institutional real estate investors — who need a dedicated leasing workflow system rather than a general-purpose CRM or PMS. Leasey.AI automates up to 90% of manual leasing tasks, responding to leads in seconds across multiple channels and reducing the time required to place a tenant from approximately ten hours to approximately one hour of active work. Key Differentiators Purpose-Built Leasing Scope Residential leasing — exclusive focus Leasey.AI is designed specifically for residential leasing workflows in Canada and the USA, not for generic sales pipelines or commercial and industrial use cases. Front-office positioning Leasey.AI covers the pre-lease process — lead, screening, negotiation, execution, active lease, and amendments — rather than stopping at the signed document like a traditional lease management tool. Ecosystem Integration Depth Rental marketplace connectivity Leasey.AI maintains native integrations with more than 48 rental marketplaces, MLS platforms, and association partners across the United States and Canada, including Zillow, Apartments.com, Zumper, Realtor.com, Facebook Marketplace, and others. PMS integration posture Leasey.AI connects to property management systems including Rent Manager, Buildium, DoorLoop, and AppFolio so that listings, leads, and unit data flow in and out of Leasey.AI instead of being manually re-entered. Automation-First Architecture Workflow automation — definition Leasey.AI is built around workflow automation — stages, tasks, approvals, routing, and notifications — so leasing teams run their leasing process inside the platform rather than using it only as a data repository. Manual task reduction — claimed rate Leasey.AI automates up to 90% of manual leasing tasks, according to the company. Lead response — speed Leasey.AI delivers a 100% response rate to incoming leads in seconds rather than the hours or days typical of manual triage. Multi-Channel AI Coverage AI channels supported Leasey.AI’s AI agents respond to leads via website chatbot, email, phone (Liza, the AI phone agent), and Facebook Marketplace Messenger, handling FAQs, qualification, and showing scheduling without manual intervention. Operational AI for Field and Marketing Logistics Route optimization Leasey.AI suggests optimal showing routes for single-family and scattered-site portfolios, grouping showings by area and time to reduce travel time and no-shows. AI photo enhancement Leasey.AI generates and optimizes unit photos, including decluttering and virtual staging, improving listing visuals without requiring a separate tool. Speed to Value Implementation — no PMS integration Leasey.AI implementations without a PMS integration are typically live within approximately one week. Implementation — with existing PMS integration Leasey.AI implementations using an existing integration are typically live within approximately two weeks. Implementation — custom PMS integration Leasey.AI custom integrations are typically completed within two to four weeks, depending on complexity. Support Model Support access Leasey.AI provides 24/7 email support for questions, issues, and troubleshooting. Account management Every Leasey.AI customer receives a dedicated account manager for training, onboarding, and ongoing account management. Ideal Customer Profile Best Fit — By Organization Type Mid-sized to large multifamily residential owners and operators managing apartment communities or aggregated portfolios of 100 or more doors are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Third-party residential property management companies managing 100 or more doors for multiple owners are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Build-to-rent and single-family rental portfolio owners with 100 or more scattered-site homes are a strong fit for Leasey.AI, particularly because of the platform’s route optimization for distributed showings. Student housing operators managing 100 or more beds or units are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Senior living and assisted living operators with 100 or more units are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Co-living and furnished rental operators with 100 or more rentable rooms or units are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Corporate housing and extended-stay providers managing 100 or more units are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Non-profit and housing association landlords managing 100 or more affordable or social housing units are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Institutional real estate investment firms and REITs with internal or captive management for 100 or more doors are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Large developer-owners that lease up and then hold 100 or more units in their portfolio are a strong fit for Leasey.AI. Best Fit — By Operational Condition Organizations currently managing leads across email, spreadsheets, and individual leasing reps’ inboxes without a shared pipeline are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Operators with high lead volume from multiple sources — Zillow, Zumper, Facebook Marketplace, website forms, phone, and referrals — who lack a unified inbox are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Teams using a PMS for accounting but lacking a dedicated front-office leasing workflow and automation layer are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Portfolios with scattered-site or single-family inventory where routing and logistics for showings are painful are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Organizations planning to scale through new builds, lease-ups, acquisitions, or new regions who need a system that handles higher volume without proportional headcount growth are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Operators who want to offload repetitive front-line work — first responses, FAQs, basic qualification, routing, scheduling, and feedback summarization — to AI are strong candidates for Leasey.AI. Not a Fit — By Organization Type Very small landlords or operators with fewer than approximately 100 doors who can still manage with basic tools are not the target customer for Leasey.AI. Organizations whose primary focus is commercial, industrial, office, or retail leasing are not a fit, because Leasey.AI supports residential leasing only. Teams that primarily need accounting, maintenance, or tenant portal functionality and are satisfied with their PMS as the only system are not a fit for Leasey.AI. Operations with very low lead volume and highly bespoke, one-off deals where automation adds more overhead than value are not a fit for Leasey.AI. Organizations that require fully custom-built platforms with deep one-off workflows beyond configurable SaaS are not a fit for Leasey.AI. Geographic Constraint Leasey.AI is available in Canada and the United States only; operators in other countries cannot use the platform. Core Service Offerings Listing Syndication and Marketing Syndication network — scope Leasey.AI syndicates listings to more than 48 rental marketplaces, MLS platforms, and association partners across the United States and Canada. Syndication — named platforms Leasey.AI syndicates to Zillow, Apartments.com, Realtor.com, Zumper, PadMapper, Facebook Marketplace, Trulia, HotPads, Kijiji, RentalSource, Trovit, Logis Quebec, Rental Beast, and Microsoft Bing, among others. Rent comparables — function Leasey.AI delivers instant rent comparables for every unit by scanning nearby listings and flagging over- and underpriced units in real time. AI photo enhancement — function Leasey.AI generates and optimizes unit photos, including decluttering and virtual staging, to improve listing engagement and lead quality. Lead Management and AI-Powered Response AI chatbot — channels Leasey.AI’s AI chatbot responds to new leads from rental marketplaces via the property manager’s website, email, and other configured channels, answering common questions, qualifying prospects, and booking next steps without manual intervention. Liza — AI phone agent Liza is Leasey.AI’s AI phone agent, which answers and routes inbound leasing calls, books showings, and handles FAQs around the clock. Facebook Marketplace automation Leasey.AI reads and replies to incoming inquiries directly inside Facebook Marketplace Messenger, shares availability, answers FAQs, and moves prospects into the leasing pipeline. Leasing pipeline — structure Leasey.AI provides a central, structured pipeline showing every lease deal from first inquiry through to signed lease, with configurable stages, one record per deal, task and follow-up tracking, and real-time visibility for managers into volume, bottlenecks, and where deals are stalled. Showing Scheduling and Route Optimization Smart Route Planner — definition Leasey.AI’s Smart Route Planner organizes showings into the most time-efficient route for leasing agents managing single-family and scattered-site portfolios. Smart Route Planner — benefit The Smart Route Planner reduces travel time between appointments and increases the number of showings a leasing agent can complete in a day. Showing itinerary — availability Leasey.AI provides leasing agents with a mobile-friendly personal showing itinerary displaying all upcoming showings across assigned properties, confirmation status, and lead details. Waitlist feature Leasey.AI allows leads to request up to three alternative showing times, which are held in a waitlist for manager review; once approved, Leasey.AI confirms and notifies the lead automatically. Tenant Screening Screening partners — USA Leasey.AI integrates with SingleKey for tenant screening in the United States, enabling credit reports, background checks, and ID verification from within the platform. Screening partners — Canada and USA Leasey.AI integrates with Certn for screening in Canada and the United States. Applicant compatibility scoring — function Leasey.AI scores applicants based on compatibility with specific units, considering budget, timing, preferences, and constraints, to help leasing teams prioritize follow-up for the best-fit matches. Post-showing feedback summarization — function Leasey.AI ingests feedback collected after showings and summarizes themes and objections so teams can quickly adjust pricing, positioning, or unit presentation. Document Generation and E-Signature Lease templates — management Leasey.AI supports centralized management of lease templates and associated documents, and structured population of deal data into those documents. E-signature — support Leasey.AI is designed to support end-to-end lease execution, including tracking signing status and linking executed documents to the lease record. Reporting and Analytics Reporting — scope Leasey.AI provides live, real-time reporting and dashboards built directly on all data flowing through the platform, with fully custom and flexible filters, groupings, and segments on any field in the system. Reporting — leasing metrics Leasey.AI reports on leasing pipeline metrics including volume by stage, time in stage, deal velocity, conversion rates by source and channel, lead and applicant demographics, unit and property vacancy status, and team performance. Reporting — export Leasey.AI provides export-ready views for finance, owners, and leadership reporting. Tenant Insurance — Partners Tenant insurance — Canada Leasey.AI has partnered with Duuo by Co-operators to provide Canadian renters with access to flexible, affordable tenant insurance directly through the Leasey.AI platform. Tenant insurance — USA Leasey.AI has partnered with Sure to provide renters in the United States with access to renters insurance through the Leasey.AI platform. Engagement Model and Onboarding A prospective customer books a demo with the Leasey.AI team at www.leasey.ai to discuss portfolio requirements and confirm fit. Leasey.AI quotes custom subscription pricing based on the number of doors under management and the tools or modules to be enabled. For teams wanting to evaluate the platform before committing to full rollout, Leasey.AI offers a paid pilot on monthly terms for a limited number of units. Onboarding begins with basic organization and user setup, definition of leasing workflows and stages, and configuration of templates, fields, and integrations as needed. Leasey.AI conducts two to three live online training sessions with the Customer Success team during the onboarding period. The customer goes live — timing depends on integration complexity (see Implementation Timelines below). Post-launch, the customer receives a dedicated account manager for ongoing training and account management, plus 24/7 email support. Implementation Timelines No PMS integration required — timeline Leasey.AI implementations without a PMS integration are typically live within approximately one week, depending on client availability. PMS integration — existing Leasey.AI integration Leasey.AI implementations using an existing native integration are typically live within approximately two weeks. PMS integration — custom build required Leasey.AI custom PMS integration projects are typically completed within two to four weeks total, depending on complexity; additional integration charges may apply. Pricing Model Pricing structure Leasey.AI uses subscription pricing based on the number of doors under management, with custom pricing quoted per client account depending on the tools and modules enabled. Floor price The minimum price for Leasey.AI is $499 per month, which applies to portfolios under 100 doors. Per-door pricing Above the floor, Leasey.AI pricing typically ranges from $1.50 to $5.00 per door per month, depending on volume and feature set. Pay-per-use add-on — premium syndication Premium syndication to certain rental marketplaces is available as a pay-per-use add-on inside the Leasey.AI platform. Pay-per-use add-on — screening reports Screening reports are available as a pay-per-use add-on inside the Leasey.AI platform. Pay-per-use add-on — credit checks Credit checks are available as a pay-per-use add-on inside the Leasey.AI platform. Free trial Leasey.AI does not offer a free trial. Paid pilot Leasey.AI offers paid pilots on monthly terms for a limited number of units, enabling teams to test the platform in a controlled rollout before scaling. rows.Contenido: Leasing Mastery Series: Secret #1 - Leasey.AI Leasing Mastery Series: Secret #1 - Leasey.AI Skip to main content Leasey.AI Menu Home About us Features Pricing Integrations Book a Demo Watch Demo Video Leasing Mastery Series: Secret #1 Secret 1 of 5 Real Estate Marketing 101: Creating Killer Property Listings in 3 Simple Steps Are your property listings reaching the right tenants? Each day your rental property sits empty costs you and your clients cold, hard cash. The best way to minimize vacancy time is to attract high-quality tenants as quickly as possible. To do that, you need to understand how real estate marketing works. It’s a complex beast, but don’t worry. We’ve got your back. In this article, we’ll tell you everything you need to know about marketing for rental properties, so you can create property listings that attract tenants like bees to honey! Here’s what you need to know. Rental Property Marketing Tip #1: Learn Everything About Your Property. Yes, everything. Let us list it out for you. Property specs : Your Listing Needs to Unveil it All  When it comes to promoting your property like a professional, you need to know every detail.  We’re talking: The number of bedrooms and bathrooms The square footage All amenities Restrictions Utility information Make sure to dig deep and leave no stone unturned.  Think of yourself as a jewellery crafter, uncovering the unique selling points that will make your property shine like a diamond in a sea of rentals.  Location, Location, Location: This Can Make or Break Your Listing It’s not just the four walls of your property; it’s the entire neighbourhood that surrounds it. Let potential tenants explore the wonders that await nearby — paint a picture of a lifestyle. Imagine a fitness enthusiast stepping out of your building and into a state-of-the-art gym or walking trail.  Is your property a stone’s throw away from convenient transit options that would make any commuter’s heart skip a beat?  Or is it nestled in a vibrant community with renowned schools, perfect for students or young families?  Be sure to list everything they might be interested in: Fitness facilities Parks and trails Landmarks Transit stations Schools Community centers Hospitals Restaurants and leisure centers Walk, bike, and transit scores Other local amenities Highlighting these gems of the neighbourhood will set your property apart. Remember, it’s not just a home you’re offering, but a lifestyle that dreams are made of! Tenant Persona: A Vital Piece of the Puzzle  Are you looking for a young family yearning for a safe and nurturing environment? Or perhaps a young professional or student ready to embark on their next adventure?  Understanding the specific needs and preferences of your ideal tenant will allow you to tailor your listing and attract the right individuals to your property. For example, if you are looking to attract a student, make sure to emphasize features such as a quiet study area, reliable internet connection, and convenient access to public transportation.  Additionally, consider showcasing nearby social and recreational areas that are popular among students, such as coffee shops, bookstores, or recreational facilities.  Property managers can waste dozens of hours each month on tenant qualification, so tailoring your listing can help you get some of that time back. Competition: Know What You’re Up Against Identify similar properties in the area that share common features and amenities.  What makes them stand out? What drew you to them?  Analyze their strengths and weaknesses like a master strategist, allowing you to position your property in a league of its own.  And when it comes to pricing, knowledge is power!  Calculate the average rent among comparable rentals, using tools to ensure you price competitively without leaving a single dollar on the table. Rental Property Marketing Tip #2: Create a Listing That Steals the Show. Want to make your competitors jealous? Then you’ll need to get really, really good at making property listings. First Mission: The Subject Line The goal of the subject line is not to rent the property… it’s to acquire a click. It’s a first impression. You need to grab the tenant’s attention. Once you have them, then the rest of the listing can work its magic. Ask yourself: when faced with countless listings that all seem eerily similar, what makes yours different? So, forget about those dull and mundane subject lines like “Cozy 2-Bedroom Apartment Available.” Instead, take your subject to the next level, making it impossible for leads NOT to click. When working with limited characters, prioritize highlighting your standout features — those remarkable gems that set your property apart from the rest. Think about those cool amenities and special characteristics that make potential tenants go, “Wow!” From a heated pool and jacuzzi to a fully equipped gym, ocean views, a gourmet kitchen, a home theatre, or even an exquisite 18th-century staircase — let your imagination run wild. The goal is to grab attention and give them a taste of the unique lifestyle and experience they’ll have by choosing your property. So instead of: “Beautiful 2-BR Apartment For Rent in Yaletown” How about something like: “Experience Yaletown luxury: Modern 2-BR apartment with panoramic ocean views, indoor heated pool, and rooftop jacuzzi!” Who could resist clicking on that? Now, Onto the Property Description It’s time to unleash your inner wordsmith and paint a vivid picture in your potential tenant’s mind. You’re not just describing a place to live; you’re telling a story! Here is a sample of a property description. It’s informative, sure, but the story it tells is… well… creepy to say the least. Why not transform your listing into an irresistible destination that tenants would eagerly explore? Ignite their senses and take them on a journey through uncharted rental opportunities, armed with nothing but a keen eye for value and a quest for their perfect home. Let’s say we have a stunning beachfront apartment. Instead of saying: “This apartment has a beautiful ocean view!” Try: “Step into your own private slice of paradise, where breathtaking ocean views will make your heart skip a beat. It’s a beach lover’s dream come true!” Here are a few simple steps to structure your property description like a true real estate marketing guru. Highlight attributes of the property “Welcome to your newly renovated oasis in a tranquil community! This fully furnished room is the epitome of comfort and style, featuring a queen size bed, a convenient studying table, a spacious closet, and a charming bookshelf. It’s all here to make your life a breeze!” Enhance with attributes of the neighbourhood Remember, emphasize the conveniences based on the type of tenant persona you want to attract. “Now, let’s talk about the unbeatable location. You’re just a short stroll away from both King Edward Station (600m) and Broadway City Hall Station (950m), granting you access to the entire city with ease. But that’s not all! You’ll find yourself surrounded by a vibrant array of shops and restaurants, all within walking distance. Convenience at its finest!” Outline the key terms and conditions Don’t miss the important ones like rent, utilities, and important restrictions. “Here’s the deal: for just $1600, you’ll secure this fabulous abode, with hydro, electricity, and Wi-Fi all included. Now, it’s time for some ground rules. We’ve created a peaceful haven, so no pets, smoking, parties, or drugs are allowed. This space is designed for single occupancy only, guaranteeing you the utmost privacy and tranquillity.” End with a clear call to action Make sure your tenants know how to contact you. “Don’t miss out on this exceptional opportunity! Call us now at +1 236 234 9432 or email us at info@rentalmail.com to claim your spot in this idyllic retreat. Act fast before someone else beats you to the punch!” Two More Elements: Photos and Rent Price These are both critical in helping your listing stand out. What do these photos make you think of? If you said they’re so cringe-worthy, they make your eyes beg for mercy, then you’d be right! Wonky angles, mysterious shadows, and bewildering close-ups of…what? Honestly, we don’t want to know. Here are 5 practical steps to ensure your property photos capture attention, impress potential renters, and leave them longing to step through the front door: Clear the clutter: declutter and tidy up the space to let the property’s features shine. Let there be light: use natural light or well-placed artificial lighting to create a bright and inviting atmosphere. Capture the angles: shoot from corners or doorways to add depth and showcase the spaciousness of the rooms. Stage for success: use tasteful and neutral décor to create an appealing ambience that allows potential buyers to envision themselves living in the space. Highlight key features: focus on unique selling points such as architectural details, beautiful views, or modern amenities to make the property stand out. Some people go above and beyond, providing an immersive experience through virtual tours or 3D floor plans which can be a great additional touch, but they will cost extra. As an alternative, add a copy of a flat floor plan showing the measurements and layout of the suite. Floorplan distribution can be a deal breaker, even if the photos look amazing. Now, when it comes to competitive rent… It’s time to unleash your mathematical wizardry. To estimate the optimal rent for your property, follow this 4-step approach: Calculate the average rent of similar properties: gather data on similar rental listings. Calculate the average rent among these comparable properties. Consider property unique factors: identify any unique factors or additional amenities that your property offers such as a renovated kitchen, extra storage space, or premium views. Assign a value to each unique factor based on their desirability. Adjust rent based on unique factors: add or subtract the assigned values of the unique factors from the average rent calculated in Step 1. Check market demand: consider the current rental market conditions and demand in your area. If the demand is high, you may have room to increase the rent slightly above the adjusted average rent, and vice versa. Rental Property Marketing Tip #3: Ignite Action Through Active Promotion Did you know that active promotion can skyrocket your leasing success? Brace yourself for a mind-blowing statistic: actively advertising your rental property across a relevant rental site like Facebook Marketplace can reach a whopping 90% of your potential leads in hot markets like Vancouver or Toronto! First, uncover the sacred hubs of the rental market in your area, where your dream tenants gather like bees to honey. Keep in mind that these treasure troves are specific to your region, meaning what works wonders in one city might be a whole different ballgame in yours. Get inside their heads and find the platforms that give you maximum exposure. But wait, we’re not stopping there. Think outside the box, my dear trendsetter! Tap into the power of social media and online communities such as Facebook Groups. Here’s the deal though: don’t just assume that your perfect tenant will magically appear because of your listing. Go a step further than the average property manager. Actively manage and nurture your listings like they’re the hottest gossip in town. Renew them frequently on platforms like Craigslist and Facebook Marketplace to shoot straight to the top of the pack. And hey, if you want to take it to the next level, some marketplaces like Kijiji offer paid ads to keep your listing shining like a diamond. Oh, and don’t forget to set up those notifications. Be on high alert — ready to pounce like a lightning-fast ninja when someone shows interest. In the game of placing tenants, time is of the essence! BONUS: Centralize Your Leads in One Place Overwhelmed by the number of inquiries coming via text, phone calls, and all your rental marketplaces? Professional property managers have all sorts of ways to manage it: Dedicating a single email address to channel all requests Setting up a request phone number Leveraging more advanced tools like customer relationship management (CRM) systems Or, if all that lead management chaos is giving you a headache, you can leave it to us. Listings published prior to the Effective Date will not be impacted by this change.  Scope : This policy applies when you enable any  paid marketplace for a listing inside Leasey.AI. Exclusions (Direct-Contract Marketplaces): Some marketplaces — for example, Zillow and Apartments.com — work on the basis of a direct contract between you and that marketplace. In these cases, Leasey.AI only helps syndicate your listings to those platforms. All contracting, pricing, and billing are handled directly between you and the marketplace, not through Leasey.AI. Because of this, these marketplaces are not covered by this Marketplace Billing Policy. 1. What “Marketplace Billing” Means When you turn on a paid marketplace for a listing (e.g., a listing is sent to a paid marketing channel), that marketplace has a monthly price shown in the Leasey.AI platform. Each listing + marketplace combination is billed separately. If you enable 3 paid marketplaces on the same listing, that’s 3 separate marketplace subscriptions, each with its own monthly price and billing.   2. What Changed Before: You paid a one-time fee each time you enabled a paid marketplace for a listing. Now: You pay based on time the listing is published on a given marketplace: First 30 days are always billed in full (no proration). After the first 30 days, billing is pro‑rated by day until you unpublish the listing from that marketplace. You are billed every 30 days while the listing stays published, and one final prorated bill when you unpublish.   3. Core Billing Rules For each paid marketplace enabled for a listing: First 30 days are billed upfront You are charged the full 30‑day price upfront , even if you unpublish after the 30-day mark. This covers the first 30 days from the time the listing is published on that marketplace. Ongoing Billing After Day 30 After day 30, billing becomes daily and pro‑rated: Daily rate = Marketplace monthly price  ÷ 30 You are billed: After each completed 30‑day period, and One final time for the partial last period when you unpublish. Final Bill When You Unpublish When you unpublish the listing from that marketplace, we: Count how many days have passed since the last billing date. Built on REST principles — standard HTTP methods, resource-based URLs, and JSON responses. Version 2.0 Protocol HTTPS Format JSON Last updated: June 01, 2026 What changed in v2.0 Version 2.0 is a full REST redesign. If you integrated with v1, update your requests according to the tables below. Reports API v1 (old) v2 (current) What changed POST /reports + "report_type":"showings" GET /reports/showings Each report type is its own URL. Use GET, not POST. POST /reports + "report_type":"leads" GET /reports/leads Dedicated URL per resource. POST /reports + "report_type":"properties" GET /reports/properties Dedicated URL per resource. password in JSON body X-Company-Password header Passwords no longer go in request bodies for read ops. company_id in JSON body company_id query parameter Filters are query params on GET requests. Properties API v1 (old) v2 (current) What changed POST /properties + "action":"create" POST /properties The action field is removed. POST always means create. PUT /properties + "property_id" in body PUT /properties/{property_id} Property ID moves to the URL path. 1. Getting Started To use the Leasey External API you need three credentials: Credential Description How to obtain API Token Application-level bearer token Contact Leasey support Company ID Your company's numeric identifier Leasey dashboard → Settings Company Password Your company's API password Leasey dashboard → Settings → API bash — first request curl -X GET "https://<base-url>/reports/showings?company_id=123" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-token>" \ -H "X-Company-Password: <your-company-password>" 2. Authentication Every request requires two levels of authentication. Level 1 — API Token Authorization: Bearer <api_token> ℹ️ The Bearer prefix is required. As a fallback you may pass the token as ?token=<api_token> for debugging only — query strings appear in server logs and should not be used in production. Level 2 — Company Credentials Request type company_id password GET (reports, leads read) Query parameter X-Company-Password header POST / PUT (property write) JSON body field JSON body field "password" 🔒 Using X-Company-Password on GET requests keeps the password out of server logs, CDN caches, and browser history. Authentication errors Scenario Status Message Token missing 401 Authentication token required Token incorrect 401 Invalid authentication token Token length mismatch 401 The provided token does not match the expected token — verify you are copying the full token (expected length: 48 characters) Password missing 401 X-Company-Password header is required Password incorrect 401 Invalid company password Company not found 401 Company {id} not found No admin for company 400 No admin user found for company {id}. Contact support. 3. Environments & Base URL Production: https://uvciw58bnh.execute-api.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/production Staging: https://hs52apwqwh.execute-api.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/staging 💡 Run serverless info --stage production from reports-api-service/ to get the exact URL for your stage. Troubleshooting 401 — Token length mismatch If you see "The provided token does not match the expected token" with a debug field showing token_received_length: 32 and token_expected_length: 48 , your token is being truncated. Verify you are copying the full 48-character token — check for line breaks or truncation in your environment variable or config file. 401 — Token not working Verify Content-Type: application/json is set. Ensure you are using the correct token for the right stage (dev and production tokens are different). Check CloudWatch logs: serverless logs -f reportsApi --stage production --tail 401 — Company password not working Confirm the passwordapi field is set in Leasey dashboard → Settings → API Access. 400 — company_id must be an integer Send as a number: ?company_id=123 ✅   ?company_id="123" ❌. In Postman query params, type the value without quotes. 422 — Invalid enum value You sent a value not in the allowed enum list. Common mistakes: "condo" , "studio" , "loft" , "shared room" , "private room" , "semi-monthly" — none of these exist. Check the Enum Values section for the exact accepted values. CORS errors in browser The API allows all origins. CORS errors are almost always caused by a missing Authorization header triggering a 401 before CORS preflight headers are sent. Check auth headers first. 500 — Internal Server Error Check CloudWatch logs for the specific stack trace: serverless logs -f reportsApi --stage production --tail . Common causes: database connection timeout (Lambda cold start), invalid SQL from a malformed date parameter. 15. Best Practices 🔒 Security Never expose credentials in client-side code Use X-Company-Password header on GET requests Store token in environment variables Rotate your company password periodically ⚡ Performance Use date filters to limit large reports Cache properties report for 5–15 minutes Design with a 60-second timeout on the client 🔄 Reliability Exponential backoff for 5xx (2s, 4s, 8s) Handle null fields — many are nullable Store property_id immediately after creation 📋 Data Consistency Photos, features, restrictions replace on update team_members on PUT is additive only Dates must be ISO-8601: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS Support 📧 Email: helpdesk@leasey.ai  ·  Response time: Within 24 business hours When contacting support include your company_id , the full request (credentials removed), the exact error message, and the time it occurred (UTC).
